mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES stays sharply below baseline, weekday trips are diverted away from discretionary shopping and dining, so RETAIL_REC remains lower over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest if the workplace drop persists rather than rebounding within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while WORKPLACES remains at least 10 points below baseline for two or more consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates people are spending more time at home, which suppresses impulse visits to shops and restaurants and pushes RETAIL_REC down within one to two weeks. If residential time at home does not remain elevated, the retail effect should not appear.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL stays above its last-4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT improves from its current depressed level by more than 5 points week-on-week, access to shopping districts strengthens and RETAIL_REC will increase over the next four weeks. This signal fails if transit recovery is temporary or concentrated in non-shopping corridors.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 5 points week-on-week from a level below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT improving by more than 5 points from below -35.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM indicates local out-of-home activity is recovering without broad consumption leakage, which should spill over into more discretionary retail trips over the next two weeks. The effect depends on PARKS not being driven by a one-off weather shock.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days when PARKS rises while GROCERY_PHARM stays within 2 points of its prior-week level.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES falls further while TRANSIT stays weak, the combined signal implies tighter movement constraints or employer caution, which suppresses discretionary shopping demand and reduces RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism is strongest if both series move in the same direction for at least two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -20 while TRANSIT remains below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES stays below -20 and TRANSIT stays below -35.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weekly improvement in PARKS during a low-transit period marks warmer outdoor conditions and higher leisure activity, which shifts some spending into nearby retail and lifts RETAIL_REC over the following week. If the park increase is not weather-driven, the signal should weaken.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points week-on-week while TRANSIT stays below -35
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the next 7 days after a >10-point PARKS increase with TRANSIT still below -35.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in GROCERY_PHARM alongside flat or worsening WORKPLACES implies necessary errand traffic is absorbing trip capacity, leaving less discretionary retail activity. Over the next four weeks, RETAIL_REC should therefore drift lower rather than recover.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated and WORKPLACES does not rebound.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES both move up together, the area is in a stay-at-home plus telework pattern that reduces discretionary outings and depresses RETAIL_REC within two weeks. The mechanism fails when higher residential time is offset by a simultaneous transit rebound.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 5 while WORKPLACES stays below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days when RESIDENTIAL is above 5 and WORKPLACES remains below -20.
